title: Slow Site Diagnosis
description: Systematically find why a WordPress site loads slowly — TTFB, database, plugins, images, and third-party scripts.

steps.title: Establish Performance Baseline
steps.instructions: Run PageSpeed Insights, GTmetrix, or WebPageTest on homepage and a heavy page. Record TTFB, LCP, and total load time to compare after fixes.

steps.title: Check Server TTFB and Hosting Tier
steps.instructions: High TTFB (>600ms) points to server, PHP, or database — not front-end assets. Review host CPU/RAM usage and consider upgrading or object caching.

steps.title: Profile Database Queries
steps.instructions: Use Query Monitor on staging to find slow or duplicate queries. Clean revisions, transients, and autoloaded options. Add indexes if a plugin queries millions of rows.

steps.title: Audit Plugin Impact Per Page
steps.instructions: Query Monitor shows per-plugin load time. Deactivate heavy plugins not needed on every page. Replace bloated plugins with lighter alternatives.

steps.title: Optimize Images and Lazy Loading
steps.instructions: Compress oversized images, serve WebP/AVIF, and enable lazy loading. Fix layout shift from images missing width/height attributes.

steps.title: Enable Page and Object Caching
steps.instructions: Configure full-page cache for anonymous visitors and Redis/Memcached for object cache. Verify cache HIT headers and correct exclusions for logged-in users.

steps.title: Audit Third-Party Scripts
steps.instructions: Defer or remove unused analytics, chat widgets, ad pixels, and social embeds. Each external script adds DNS lookup and blocking time.

steps.title: Re-test and Document Improvements
steps.instructions: Re-run the same performance tests. Document changes made and set a monitoring alert if load time regresses.
